author: Jesus of Nazareth
text: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find.

author: Jesus of Nazareth
text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

author: Jesus of Nazareth
text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

author: Paul the Apostle
text: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

author: Hebrew Bible
text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

author: Hebrew Bible
text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

author: Hebrew Bible
text: What doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

author: Qur’an
text: There is no compulsion in religion.

author: Qur’an
text: With hardship comes ease.

author: Qur’an
text: We made you into nations and tribes so that you may know one another.

author: Dhammapada
text: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased.

author: Dhammapada
text: To avoid all evil, to cultivate good, and to cleanse one’s mind—this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

author: Laozi
source: Tao Te Ching, chapter 1 (English rendering; translations vary)
text: The Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao.

author: Laozi
source: Tao Te Ching, chapter 64 (English rendering; translations vary)
text: A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath one’s feet.

author: Bhagavad Gita
text: You have the right to work, but not to the fruits of work.

author: Socrates (as portrayed by Plato)
text: The unexamined life is not worth living.

author: Aristotle
source: Metaphysics, Book I (English rendering; translations vary)
text: All men by nature desire to know.

author: Epictetus
text: Some things are in our control and others not.

author: Marcus Aurelius
text: Men seek retreats for themselves, houses in the country, sea-shores, and mountains.

author: René Descartes
source: Discourse on the Method, Part IV (English translation)
text: I think, therefore I am.

author: Francis Bacon
text: Knowledge is power.

author: John Locke
source: An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book II, chapter 1
text: Let us then suppose the mind to be, as we say, white paper, void of all characters.

author: David Hume
source: An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, Section XII
text: A wise man, therefore, proportions his belief to the evidence.

author: Immanuel Kant
source: An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment? (English translation)
text: Dare to know!

author: Mary Wollstonecraft
source: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792)
text: I do not wish them to have power over men; but over themselves.

author: Henry David Thoreau
source: Walden, “Where I Lived, and What I Lived For”
text: Our life is frittered away by detail. Simplify, simplify.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
text: Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.

author: Friedrich Nietzsche
source: Twilight of the Idols, “Maxims and Arrows” 8 (English translation)
text: What does not kill me makes me stronger.

author: Bertrand Russell
source: The Problems of Philosophy (1912), concluding chapter
text: Philosophy is to be studied, not for the sake of any definite answers to its questions.

author: Isaac Newton
text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.

author: Isaac Newton
text: I frame no hypotheses.

author: Charles Darwin
text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.

author: Charles Darwin
text: There is grandeur in this view of life.

author: Michael Faraday
text: Nothing is too wonderful to be true, if it be consistent with the laws of nature.

author: Louis Pasteur
source: Lecture at University of Lille (1854; English translation)
text: In the fields of observation chance favors only the prepared mind.

author: Ada Lovelace
text: The Analytical Engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything.

author: Galileo Galilei
text: The universe ... is written in the language of mathematics.

author: William Shakespeare
text: There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.

author: William Shakespeare
source: The Tempest, Act IV, Scene I
text: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.

author: William Shakespeare
source: As You Like It, Act II, Scene VII
text: All the world’s a stage.

author: William Blake
text: To see a World in a Grain of Sand.

author: William Blake
source: The Marriage of Heaven and Hell
text: If the doors of perception were cleansed every thing would appear to man as it is, infinite.

author: John Keats
text: Beauty is truth, truth beauty.

author: Percy Bysshe Shelley
text: Poets are the unacknowledged legislators of the world.

author: Emily Dickinson
text: Tell all the truth but tell it slant —

author: Walt Whitman
text: I contain multitudes.

author: Oscar Wilde
source: The Picture of Dorian Gray, Preface
text: All art is quite useless.

author: Leo Tolstoy
text: Art is a human activity consisting in this, that one man consciously, by means of certain external signs, hands on to others feelings he has lived through.
